  MEETING OF THE
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 1, 2021 AT 7:00 P.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Community interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 1st Monday of every month.

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact
the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-0705 prior
to the meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the Public Safety Commission may teleconference into the meeting without noticing
each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
As a precaution to protect staff, our constituents, and appointed officials, the City is following
the State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer recommendations to prevent
and reduce transmission of COVID0-19 by holding meetings via teleconference

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to fire@cityofsanmarino.org before or during
  the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read by the
  Committee during public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the
  interest of time.

  Meeting ID: 862 3975 2807

  Meeting ID: 862 3975 2807

  3) Submitting Public Comment

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200
Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation
Department, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website:

FROM:  Police Chief John N Incontro
BY:  Vanessa Guillen, Administrative Assistant

DATE:  November 1, 2021

SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT SEPTEMBER 2021

BACKGROUND

Each month the Police Department provides a brief update on crime, traffic issues, and other
items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

This report will provide the Public Safety Commission with information for the month of
September 2021. The Pandemic has resulted in altering police service in our community. We
have had to modify the department’s community engagement, neighborhood watch programs,
and limited our contact with others to lessen the potential of infection spread. The services at
the front desk have been curtailed, limiting one on one contact, other than emergencies or
reporting of serious crimes.

As of September 30, 2021, Part 1 crimes have overall decreased by 20.57% when compared to
September 2020. The city suffered eleven larcenies in September, related to thefts from
unlocked vehicles, gardening equipment, and thefts by fraud. The city suffered twelve residential
burglaries and one arrest was made related to two of the residential burglaries.

INVESTIGATIVE FOLLOW-UP

As of September 30, 2021 the Detective Bureau completed the following activates;
  • The Detective Bureau filed 10 cases for prosecution with the Alhambra District
  Attorney’s Office.
  • Three search warrants were obtained for ongoing investigations.

  Page 5 of 33
 COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT

With continued COVID-19 concerns, the department has had to limit their community
engagement. During the month of September, the Police Department hosted a virtual
Neighborhood Watch meeting via Zoom.

PERSONNEL UPDATE

The department currently has 28 of the 30 sworn positions filled. The department has two
sworn position vacancies and one cadet position vacancies.

TECHNOLOGY

The Flock Safety Cameras installed throughout the City have assisted in alerting officers to
stolen vehicles through the city, for the month of September the Flock Safety Cameras assisted
in one arrest.

TRAFFIC REPORT

A radar traffic trailer was placed at three separate intersections during the month of
September. From September 1 to September 18, the trailer was placed at the intersections of
Ridgeway Road and Lorain Road, from September 19 to September 20, it was placed at Los
Robles Avenue and Mission Street, and from September 21 to September 30, it was placed at
the intersections of San Marino Avenue and Sherwood Road.

Traffic enforcement is based upon three areas; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list
of traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our
traffic collision investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory
factor in the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.
The traffic data utilized for traffic enforcement are the top five locations for traffic collisions and
the top Primary Collision Factors (PCF’s), or causes of the traffic collisions.

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT REPORT

MONTHLY PERFORMANCE METRICS
Since the last Public Safety Commission Meeting, the Fire Department has submitted the
September Monthly Performance Metrics to the City Council. A copy of the report has been
included in this update. The report includes the number of responses made by the Department,
training hours, Fire Prevention inspections, and the Department’s cardiac arrest performance for
the month of September.

COVID-19 RESPONSE
San Marino Fire Department personnel continue to follow department personal protective
equipment protocols during emergencies for the safety of firefighters and patients. Additionally,
paramedics follow all current Los Angeles County Department of Health Services protocols for
the evaluation and transportation of patients requiring emergency medical services.

As of October 21, 2021, 86.5% of San Marino residents age 12 and older have received at least
one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Additionally, 98.7% of youth age 12-17 and 99.2% of San
Marino residents age 65 and older have received at least one dose.
Residents who received their COVID-19 vaccination within the State of California may request
a digital copy of their COVID-19 vaccine record by visiting https://myvaccinerecord.cdph.ca.gov/.

MOBILE VACCINATION PROGRAM
The San Marino Fire Department has completed distribution of vaccines to residents as part of
the Homebound 65+ Vaccination Program. The vaccine booster is now widely available, and a
number of our residents have taken advantage of the opportunity. The Department was able to
provide boosters of the Pfizer vaccine to 24 residents who were unable to leave their home.

SIGNIFICANT INCIDENTS
On October 17, Investigator 9 Jason Sutliff and Investigator 91 Michael White assisted the Pasadena
Fire Department with a spree of arson related incidents in the city of Pasadena. At approximately
6:00 p.m., the Pasadena Fire Department responded to a residential structure fire on the 300 block

  Page 11 of 33
 of North Chester Avenue. After arriving on scene, the first responding Pasadena engine reported
heavy fire from a separate structure one block to the east. Engine 91 was dispatched as an additional
resource for both incidents. San Marino Investigators 9 and 91 were the first Verdugo Fire
Investigation Task Force members on scene and were assigned the incident. Three additional fires
were then reported a few blocks away. Additional investigators from Pasadena, South Pasadena,
Monrovia, and Montebello were called to assist with the investigations of the five incidents.

San Marino investigators determined the first two fires to be incendiary. The Pasadena Police
Department successfully apprehended a suspect during an unrelated traffic stop. The suspect
admitted to setting the fires and was placed under arrest.

Strike Team Deployments

On October 5, Firefighter/Paramedic Dave Tannehill was dispatched as part of a mutual aid response
to the Dixie Fire in Plumas County, CA where he was assigned as a Fireline Paramedic working with
hand crews on the fireline. Firefighter Tannehill returned on October 26, 2021. The Dixie Fire
started on July 13, 2021 and was determined to be 100% contained on October 26, 2021. The Dixie
Fire is the largest single wildfire in California state history.

TRAINING
Fire Department personnel participated in an estimated 270 hours of training during the month
of October. Final training hours will be included in the October Performance Metrics Report.
The Department currently has 4 probationary firefighters, and training efforts continue to focus
almost exclusively on Probationary Firefighter training.
Training during the month of September included continuing EMS education with the UCLA
Nurse Educator, incident command systems, forcible entry, ventilation, and elevator rescue.

On October 21, the San Marino Fire Department conducted an earthquake drill with members
of the City’s Executive Team as part of the annual “Great Shake Out” drill. Fire Chief Rueda
reviewed the City’s Emergency Operations Plan and Earthquake specific procedures. Mr. James
Featherstone, a former member of the Los Angeles Fire Department, General Manager of the
Los Angeles Emergency Management Department, Executive Director of the Homeland Security
Advisory Council, and current Executive Director of Themata Strategic, LLC, led the exercise
that simulated a 7.4 earthquake along the southern San Andreas Fault. Executive members
participated in several potential scenarios of damage caused by a catastrophic event, including
loss of power and gas main ruptures.

  Page 12 of 33
 WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS
As the fire season begins in Southern California, moderate to severe drought continues to persist
across our region. So far, our region has seen well below normal fire activity. However,
beginning this month, live fuel moistures in Los Angeles County have just reached critical levels.
The fire department is wrapping up brush inspections in our Very High Fire Severity Zone to
ensure that in the event of a fire in our City, the Firefighters have every opportunity to save life
and property. Further information on our vegetation management program can be obtained at
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org/brushclearance.

EARTHQUAKE RETROFITTING GRANTS
The application period for the CEA Earthquake Brace & Bolt Program grants for seismic retrofit
of older homes is now open. Earthquake Brace + Bolt (EBB) helps homeowners lessen the
potential for damage during an earthquake. EBB offers a grant of up to $3,000 toward a seismic
retrofit for qualifying older houses. Visit https://www.earthquakebracebolt.com to sign up to be
notified when registration opens.

RESCUE AMBULANCE 91
Members of the San Marino Fire Department visited the Republic EVS manufacturing plant in
Elkhart, Indiana as part of a final inspection of the RA 791 replacement vehicle. The RA 791
replacement was originally scheduled to be completed in Spring 2021. However, due to
manufacturing setbacks caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the estimated delivery date was
extended to Autumn 2021.

FY 2021-22 DEPARTMENT OBJECTIVES
  •  Continue to lead the City’s response to COVID-19.
  •  Continue to provide accurate measurements of Fire Department performance.
  •  Place into service new Rescue Ambulance 91.
  •  Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  •  Develop a City-wide Evacuation Plan for review and approval by the Disaster Council
  and City Council.

  Page 13 of 33
  •  Improve the City’s Emergency Preparedness through the completion of the upgrade to
  the Emergency Operations Center, including new phone and computer set up, new
  mapping, and staff training.
 •  Review and revise the City’s Emergency Operations Plan for City Council adoption.
 •  Conduct a City-wide emergency operations exercise with City staff, Department Heads,
  and the School District.
 •  Complete necessary upgrades to the Emergency Operations Center in coordination
  with the Parks and Public Works Department.

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY PERFORMANCE REPORT

The attached San Marino Fire Department September 2021 Performance Report represents the
incident data reports intended to meet the Improvement Goals referenced in the March 2, 2018
Report to City Council titled; Implementation Plan Fire Department Deployment Study. The
Fire Department has been working closely with Verdugo Fire Dispatch (VFD) to ensure the
accuracy of the data being reported. Some of the data sets are not currently available from VFD
and are listed as N/A. VFD has been made aware of the San Marino Fire Department’s interest
in pursuing the data associated with the fire and life safety goals as approved by the City Council.
Improvement Goal A in the Report recommended the following:

Call Processing Goals
9-1-1 calls will be answered at the primary PSAP (Public Safety Answering Point) San Marino
Police Department within 15 seconds, 95% of the time.

9-1-1 calls will be transferred from the primary PSAP to Verdugo Fire Dispatch within 30 seconds
from the time answered, 95% of the time.
This data is not available.

Recommended Turnout Goal
Response personnel shall initiate the response of a unit capable of mitigating an incident to a
priority fire and rescue incident 80 seconds from notification 90% of the time.

Response personnel shall initiate response to all other priority incidents within 60 seconds from
notification 90% of the time.

Recommended First-Due Response Time Goal
The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at a priority
fire or rescue incident within 5 minutes and 20 seconds from notification of response personnel,
90 percent of the time.

  Page 15 of 33
 The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at all other
priority incidents within 5 minutes from notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.

Recommended Response Force Goal
The full effective response force shall arrive at a moderate risk structure fire within 9 minutes
and 20 seconds of notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.
This data is not available.

Cardiac Arrest Data
The Cardiac Arrest data set includes the total number of cardiac arrest patients treated by
Firefighter/Paramedics. We always pray that the number is as low as possible. The more
important data sets are the subsequent measures which include the number of times the
Firefighter/Paramedics are successful in returning a patient’s spontaneous circulation (ROSC) –
our goal with ROSC is always 100%. Saving lives is why the Fire Department exists; unfortunately,
this is not always in our control. Lastly, the subsequent data sets measure the percentages of
correct treatments performed by the Firefighter/Paramedics.

San Marino Fire Department Quarterly Report
As of July 2018, a Quarterly Report has been added to help in identifying trends in the data being
provided. This report includes the third quarter of 2021.

City of San Marino COVID-19 Response
San Marino Fire Department personnel continue to follow department personal protective
equipment protocols during emergencies for the safety of firefighters and patients. Additionally,
paramedics follow all current Los Angeles County Department of Health Services protocols for
the evaluation and transportation of patients requiring emergency medical services.

As of October 14, 2021, 86.2% of San Marino residents age 12 and older have received at least
one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Additionally, 98.4% of youth age 12-17 and 99.0% of San
Marino residents age 65 and older have received at least one dose.

The San Marino Fire Department has started distribution of COVID-19 booster vaccinations for
homebound residents age 65+ who participated in our initial vaccination program in April 2021.
The City’s Resident Support Hotline has reached out to previous program recipients to schedule
appointments.

Overtime
As of July 18, 2021 the Fire Department has achieved full staffing. During the month of
September, the Fire Department dispatched one Firefighter Field Observer to the Dixie Fire and

  Page 16 of 33
 one engine to the Caldor Fire, resulting in 1,232 hours of overtime. Mutual Aid overtime is 100%
reimbursed by the State of California.

SUBJECT:  DISCUSSION CONCERNING POSSIBLE POLICE DEPARTMENT
  BEARD AND TATTOO POLICIES

BACKGROUND

In an effort to increase recruitment and retention of police officers, the department is exploring
the idea of approving the wearing of beards and display of tattoos by department sworn
personnel.

DISCUSSION

Throughout law enforcement the approval of officers to display tattoos and wear beards is
becoming more common. For the department, recruitment has been difficult and retention is a
serious issue. This is not an issue unique to this department but to departments throughout
the Country. The wearing of beards and having tattoos are more common with the age group
that we are focusing our recruitment efforts.

The policy that we have developed is similar to the Glendale Police Department. Their policies
have been adapted for our purposes. The department is requesting the Public Safety
Commission to discuss and provide suggestions concerning these two possible policies. The
two policies are attached for your review.

FISCAL IMPACT

None

 TO:  All Police Department Personnel

FROM:  John Incontro, Chief of Police

DATE:  November 1, 2021

SUBJECT:  DRAFT BEARD POLICY

PURPOSE

The purpose of this policy is to update the department’s policy regarding facial hair.

FACIAL HAIR

A goatee or full beard and mustache may be worn. The goatee or full beard and mustache shall
be no longer than a 3/8 inch in length, evenly and neatly trimmed, and must not extend in length
beyond the normal contours of the face. An employee's facial hair is subject to supervisor
determination as to whether it is in compliance with policy.

  •  Any officer choosing to wear facial hair must pass the annual gas mask fit test.

  •  Any employee choosing to wear a goatee or beard must have shaving materials available,
  in the event of an emergency or other event, as determined by the Chief, where facial
  hair may not be worn.

  •  Beards or goatees are not allowed to be worn by any officer on training.

The implementation of this policy will be reviewed by the Chief periodically to ensure compliance
with the policy.

  Page 31 of 33
 TO:  All Police Department Personnel

FROM:  John Incontro, Chief of Police

DATE:  November 1, 2021

SUBJECT:  DRAFT TATTOO POLICY

PURPOSE

The purpose of this policy is to update the department’s policy regarding visible tattoos.

DISPLAY OF VISIBLE TATTOOS

This Policy provides for the display of tattoos in public by department personnel. It sets the
standard for what is permissible and most importantly what type of tattoos are prohibited. Visible
tattoos or body art are strictly prohibited above the neckline of a standard uniform t-shirt or
below the wrist. In addition, the following are strictly prohibited whether the tattoo or body
marking is visible or not:

  1. Extremist: tattoos or body markings that are affiliated with, depicting, or symbolizing
  extremist philosophies, organizations, or activities. Extremist philosophies, organizations,
  and activities are those which advocate hatred or intolerance based on race, ethnicity,
  national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, economic status, age,
  or disability; advocate, create, or engage in illegal discrimination based on race, ethnicity,
  national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, economic status, age
  or disability; or advocate violence or other unlawful means of depriving individuals rights
  under the U.S. Constitution, California Constitution, and Federal or State law.

  2. Indecent: tattoos or body markings that depict nudity or are offensive to modesty,
  decency, propriety, or professionalism.

  3. Racist: tattoos or body markings that advocate a philosophy that degrades or demeans a
  person or group of people based on race, ethnicity, or national origin.

  4. Sexist: tattoos or body markings that advocate a philosophy that degrades or demeans a
  person or group of people based on gender.

  Page 32 of 33
 5. Tattoos or body markings that are contrary to the purpose of law enforcement including,
  but not limited to, depictions symbolizing or indicative of narcotics, illegal or gang related
  activity, or symbols suggestive of activity that undermines the purpose of law enforcement.

6. Group tattoos if the theme, message, content, or mere existence as a group tattoo or
  marking is viewed by the Chief of Police or designee to be in conflict with the
  Department’s mission, professional image, or is otherwise in violation with any other part
  of this policy.

APPROVAL OF TATTOOS

Department employees who wish to display visible tattoos or body markings while on duty
shall submit a signed certification to the Chief of Police via the chain of command that the
tattoo or body marking to be displayed does not violate this policy.

CHIEF OF POLICE REVIEW

The Chief of Police reserves the right to require employees to conceal their tattoos or body
markings if deemed necessary to comport with evolving community standards, attitudes, or
beliefs.

Further, the Chief of Police shall make the final determination on whether a tattoo or body
marking violates this policy. Such determination is not subject to appeal.

Factors the Chief of Police may consider in making a determination regarding a tattoo or
body marking include, but are not limited to, the following:

(a) Whether symbols or markings are likely to elicit a strong negative reaction in the
community and the workplace.
